rationale: Young-Burgess classification is the primary management-guiding system for pelvic fractures; AP-compression vs lateral-compression vs vertical-shear directs resuscitation and fixation strategy.

The sequence of haemorrhage-control decision-making — binder → resuscitation → angioembolisation vs pre-peritoneal packing vs REBOA — is the core management principle for this SDL; testing the role of angioembolisation in the haemodynamically unstable patient clarifies a common misconception.
Open pelvic fractures carry the highest mortality; recognising which structures elevate them to an open injury and the mandatory surgical steps (faecal diversion) is a high-yield OR trap question.

ASIA impairment scale is the universal neurological grading tool for spinal cord injury; correctly assigning a grade determines prognosis and surgical urgency — ASIA A (complete) vs D (incomplete) is the highest-yield distinction.
The log-roll technique requires exactly 4 people in the correct roles; students commonly miscount or misassign the leader position — testing this directly reinforces the clinical skill block.
TLICS scoring drives the surgical vs non-surgical decision in spinal injuries; a score ≥5 is a surgical threshold — calculating it for a clinical scenario tests integrative application.
